title: Downtime capture app in Power Apps: start and stop events with reason codes on a SharePoint list
summary: A canvas app where operators start a machine stop in two taps, pick a reason, and close it later with the duration calculated by DateDiff. Includes data model, Power Fx, a worked availability example and delegation notes.
body:
Most plants lose downtime data in the gap between the machine stopping and somebody typing it into a spreadsheet at the end of the shift. This canvas app lets an operator start a downtime event with two taps, pick a reason, and close it later with the duration calculated automatically. Everything lands in one SharePoint list that Power BI, Excel or Power Automate can read. It is a capture tool, not an OEE system: it gives you clean stop events with start, end, reason and machine, which is the raw material for availability and Pareto analysis.

## Prerequisites and version

- Power Apps canvas app (phone or tablet layout) with the SharePoint connector, which is a standard connector. Check your license and tenant policy before you rely on it.
- Two SharePoint lists on a site your operators can edit. Column types matter, so create them exactly as listed below.
- Formulas below use only core Power Fx functions (Patch, Defaults, Filter, SortByColumns, DateDiff, IfError, Notify, Set, UpdateContext, Navigate). Verify the formula bar shows no red underline after you rename controls.
- Choice values are written as a record such as `{ Value: "Open" }` in the formulas below. That is the shape commonly used for SharePoint Choice columns, but the Learn Patch page documents only Dataverse enums and says other data sources "might require different record shapes". Test one Patch against your own list before you build the rest, and check in the formula bar.

## Data model

List `Machines` (read-only for operators): `Title` (machine code, single line of text, unique by convention), `Line` (text), `Active` (Yes/No).

List `Downtimes`:

| Column | Type | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Title | Single line of text | Filled by the app: machine code plus start time |
| MachineCode | Single line of text | Copy of Machines.Title, not a lookup, so Patch stays simple and filters stay delegable |
| Reason | Choice | Example values: Breakdown, Changeover, Material shortage, Quality hold, Planned maintenance, No operator |
| StartTime | Date and time | Include time |
| EndTime | Date and time | Blank while the stop is open |
| DurationMin | Number | Written when the event is closed |
| Status | Choice | Open, Closed |
| ReportedBy | Single line of text | User().Email |
| Comment | Multiple lines of text | Plain text |

## Screens

1. `scrOpen`: gallery of open stops, button "New stop".
2. `scrStart`: dropdown for machine, dropdown for reason, button "Start stop".
3. `scrClose`: shows the selected stop, a comment box, button "Machine running again".

## Formulas

Machine dropdown on `scrStart` (`ddMachine.Items`):

```powerfx
SortByColumns(Filter(Machines, Active = true), "Title", SortOrder.Ascending)
```

Reason dropdown (`ddReason.Items`) reads the choices from the column definition:

```powerfx
Choices(Downtimes.Reason)
```

Gallery of open stops on `scrOpen` (`galOpen.Items`):

```powerfx
SortByColumns(
    Filter(Downtimes, Status.Value = "Open"),
    "StartTime", SortOrder.Descending
)
```

Start button (`btnStart.OnSelect`):

```powerfx
IfError(
    Patch(
        Downtimes,
        Defaults(Downtimes),
        {
            Title: ddMachine.Selected.Title & " " & Text(Now(), "yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm"),
            MachineCode: ddMachine.Selected.Title,
            Reason: { Value: ddReason.Selected.Value },
            StartTime: Now(),
            Status: { Value: "Open" },
            ReportedBy: User().Email
        }
    ),
    Notify("The stop was not saved: " & FirstError.Message, NotificationType.Error),
    Notify("Stop started", NotificationType.Success);
    Navigate(scrOpen, ScreenTransition.None)
)
```

Elapsed minutes in the gallery (label inside `galOpen`, `lblElapsed.Text`). The `varTick` variable is refreshed by a Timer control so the label updates. Put the Timer on `scrOpen` (Learn: `AutoStart` starts the timer when the user navigates to the screen that contains it), set `Duration` to 60000 (milliseconds), `Repeat` and `AutoStart` to true, and `OnTimerEnd` to `Set(varTick, Now())`:

```powerfx
DateDiff(ThisItem.StartTime, Coalesce(varTick, Now()), TimeUnit.Minutes) & " min"
```

Close button on `scrClose` (`btnClose.OnSelect`), where `galOpen.Selected` is the chosen stop:

```powerfx
IfError(
    Patch(
        Downtimes,
        galOpen.Selected,
        {
            EndTime: Now(),
            Status: { Value: "Closed" },
            DurationMin: DateDiff(galOpen.Selected.StartTime, Now(), TimeUnit.Minutes),
            Comment: txtComment.Text
        }
    ),
    Notify("Could not close the stop: " & FirstError.Message, NotificationType.Error),
    Notify("Stop closed", NotificationType.Success);
    Back()
)
```

Total minutes closed today for one machine, for a small KPI label. The Filter is delegable, the Sum then runs on the rows that came back, so keep the window small:

```powerfx
Sum(
    Filter(Downtimes, MachineCode = ddMachine.Selected.Title, StartTime >= Today()),
    DurationMin
)
```

## Worked example (invented data)

Press 07 stops at 06:12 with reason "Material shortage". The operator taps New stop, selects the machine and reason, and the app writes StartTime 06:12 and Status Open. The material arrives and the machine runs again at 06:47. The operator opens the stop and taps "Machine running again". DateDiff returns 35, so DurationMin is 35 and Status is Closed. Later that shift the same press has a 10 minute changeover and a 20 minute breakdown. The KPI label shows 35 + 10 + 20 = 65 minutes. If the planned production time for the shift was 450 minutes, availability from these stops is (450 - 65) / 450 = 85.6 percent. Treat that as an example of the arithmetic, not as a benchmark.

## How to adapt

- More reasons: add choices to the column, the dropdown follows automatically. Keep the list short (under ten); long lists make operators choose "Other".
- Reason hierarchy (loss category and detail): add a second Choice column and filter its dropdown by the first only if you really use both levels in analysis.
- Barcode or QR on the machine: replace the machine dropdown by a scanner control, see the tool crib entry for the pattern.
- Alerts for long stops: let Power Automate watch the list for Status Open longer than your threshold; do not poll from the app.
- Dataverse: replace the lists with tables; Choice values then use the enumeration syntax of your table, check the column names in the formula bar.

## Common mistakes

- Using a lookup column for the machine. Patching lookups needs a record with Id and Value, and filtering on lookup subfields is limited. A text copy is simpler and good enough.
- Forgetting to wrap Patch in IfError. Without it a permission or network error silently leaves the stop unsaved while the operator believes it was recorded.
- Calculating duration with Now() on the device and expecting it to match another time zone. SharePoint stores date and time values in UTC and Power Apps shows local time; DateDiff between two values that both went through the same conversion is safe, but check your site regional settings if numbers look shifted by an hour.
- Showing a total with Sum over the whole list. The SharePoint delegation table does not list Sum, so assume it runs on the rows that came back; always put a delegable Filter inside it.
- Reading DateDiff as exact elapsed time. DateDiff returns a whole number of units, and the Learn examples for larger units look like boundary counting, not truncated elapsed time. For minutes, test with timestamps whose seconds differ, or use `TimeUnit.Seconds` and divide by 60 if you need exact minutes.
- Leaving stops open when an operator goes home. Add a supervisor view of old open stops and a rule for who closes them.

## Delegation notes

- According to the SharePoint delegation table on Learn, `=` on a complex (Choice) column works through its subfield, comparisons on Date and time columns are delegable, and `Today()` is sent to the source as a constant. SortByColumns on a normal column is delegable; sorting on the Choice column itself is not.
- The same table says `Not` and `IsBlank` do not delegate to SharePoint (`= Blank()` is the delegable form for equality). It does not list Sum or CountRows, so expect a delegation warning and keep the Filter in front. Check the formula bar for warnings and test with more than 2,000 rows before roll-out, because demo data hides the problem.
- The default data row limit is 500 and can be raised in the app settings (the current delegation overview names 10,000 as the maximum). Treat that as a safety net, not as a design.

## Privacy and safety

- ReportedBy links stop events to a person. In many countries a works council or data protection officer must agree before you evaluate by person. Consider removing the column and keeping only the machine and shift.
- Downtime reasons are typed by people under time pressure; do not use them as proof for disciplinary matters.
- The app does not replace the safety procedures of the plant. If a stop is a safety event, follow your reporting process; the app is only a log.

title: 5S audit app in Power Apps with pillar scores saved to SharePoint
summary: A tablet questionnaire for 5S audits: questions come from a list, ratings are scored per pillar and overall, and every answer is stored as a row for trending. Power Fx, data model and a worked 54 of 80 example.
body:
A paper 5S audit sheet gets filled in once, filed, and never trended. This canvas app turns the audit into a short questionnaire on a tablet, scores each pillar (Sort, Set in order, Shine, Standardise, Sustain), and stores every answer as a row so you can compare areas and months. The questions live in a list, so the lean team can change them without touching the app.

## Prerequisites and version

- Power Apps canvas app, SharePoint connector (standard connector; check your license).
- Three SharePoint lists, described below.
- The scale 0 to 4 per question is a convention used in this example, not a standard. Define your own scale in the audit guide and print it next to the questions, otherwise two auditors will score the same area differently.

## Data model

List `Questions5S`: `Title` (the question, for example "Only items needed for the current job are on the workbench"), `Pillar` (single line of text, one of Sort, Set in order, Shine, Standardise, Sustain), `Active` (Yes/No).

List `Audits5S` (one row per audit): `Title` (area name), `AuditDate` (date), `Auditor` (single line of text, email), `ScorePercent` (number). The lowest pillar is not stored; derive it in reports from `AuditLines`.

List `AuditLines` (one row per answered question): `Title` (question text copy), `AuditId` (number, holds the Audits5S ID), `Pillar` (text), `Rating` (number 0 to 4), `Comment` (multiple lines of text).

Storing the question text in each line keeps old audits readable after the question list changes.

## Formulas

Start of an audit (`btnStartAudit.OnSelect`): copy the active questions into a local collection with an unrated marker of -1.

```powerfx
ClearCollect(
    colLines,
    AddColumns(
        Filter(Questions5S, Active = true),
        "Rating", -1,
        "Note", ""
    )
);
Navigate(scrQuestions, ScreenTransition.None)
```

Rating dropdown inside the gallery that shows `colLines` (`ddRating.Items`, `ddRating.OnChange`):

```powerfx
// ddRating.Items
[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]

// ddRating.OnChange
UpdateIf(colLines, ID = ThisItem.ID, { Rating: ddRating.Selected.Value })
```

`UpdateIf` works on collections and matches the SharePoint ID column that came along from `Questions5S`.

Progress label (`lblProgress.Text`):

```powerfx
CountRows(Filter(colLines, Rating >= 0)) & " of " & CountRows(colLines) & " answered"
```

Overall score in percent, only over answered questions, as a named value (put it in a label or in `OnSelect` of the save button):

```powerfx
With(
    { answered: Filter(colLines, Rating >= 0) },
    If(
        CountRows(answered) = 0,
        0,
        Round(Sum(answered, Rating) / (CountRows(answered) * 4) * 100, 1)
    )
)
```

Score per pillar for a summary table (`galPillars.Items`):

```powerfx
ForAll(
    ["Sort", "Set in order", "Shine", "Standardise", "Sustain"] As p,
    {
        Pillar: p.Value,
        Score: Sum(Filter(colLines, Pillar = p.Value), Rating),
        MaxPoints: CountRows(Filter(colLines, Pillar = p.Value)) * 4
    }
)
```

Save button (`btnSave.OnSelect`). The button is disabled unless every question is rated: set `DisplayMode` to `If(CountIf(colLines, Rating < 0) = 0, DisplayMode.Edit, DisplayMode.Disabled)`. The score is set first, then the header, then the lines. Failures of single lines are collected inside the loop with `IfError` into a helper collection `colFailed` (created by the first `Collect`), because the Learn page for `Errors()` says its information is cleared by later data functions on the same data source and has no `ForAll` example.

```powerfx
Set(
    varScore,
    With(
        { answered: Filter(colLines, Rating >= 0) },
        If(
            CountRows(answered) = 0,
            0,
            Round(Sum(answered, Rating) / (CountRows(answered) * 4) * 100, 1)
        )
    )
);
Set(
    varAudit,
    Patch(
        Audits5S,
        Defaults(Audits5S),
        {
            Title: ddArea.Selected.Value,
            AuditDate: Today(),
            Auditor: User().Email,
            ScorePercent: varScore
        }
    )
);
If(
    IsError(varAudit),
    Notify("The audit header was not saved.", NotificationType.Error),
    Clear(colFailed);
    ForAll(
        colLines,
        IfError(
            Patch(
                AuditLines,
                Defaults(AuditLines),
                {
                    Title: ThisRecord.Title,
                    AuditId: varAudit.ID,
                    Pillar: ThisRecord.Pillar,
                    Rating: ThisRecord.Rating,
                    Comment: ThisRecord.Note
                }
            ),
            Collect(colFailed, { Line: ThisRecord.Title, Msg: FirstError.Message })
        )
    );
    If(
        IsEmpty(colFailed),
        Notify("Audit saved", NotificationType.Success); Navigate(scrHome),
        Notify(CountRows(colFailed) & " lines were not saved. Do not close the app, tap Save again only after reading the note below, or call the lean team.", NotificationType.Warning)
    )
)
```

Check in your own app, with a forced failure (for example by removing the user's edit permission on a test list), that `colFailed` fills as expected; the Learn pages do not describe this combination of `IfError`, `Collect` and `ForAll` end to end. If a line failed, tapping Save again would duplicate the header, so in production move the header Patch to a separate step and keep `varAudit` until the lines are confirmed.

## Worked example (invented data)

Area "Assembly cell 3", 20 questions, 4 per pillar, maximum 80 points. Scores: Sort 14 of 16, Set in order 11 of 16, Shine 12 of 16, Standardise 9 of 16, Sustain 8 of 16. Total 54 of 80, so the overall score is 54 / 80 x 100 = 67.5 percent. Per pillar that is 87.5, 68.8, 75.0, 56.3 and 50.0 percent. The weakest pillar is Sustain, which usually means the area was cleaned for the audit but has no routine. The follow-up is a management question (who owns the weekly check), not a clean-up event.

## How to adapt

- Weights: add a Number column `Weight` to `Questions5S` and use `Sum(answered, Rating * Weight)` over `Sum(answered, 4 * Weight)`.
- Photo evidence: add an Attachments card in an edit form on the comment screen, or use the Gemba walk entry's pattern.
- Trends: build a Power BI report on `Audits5S` and `AuditLines`; the pillar score is a simple grouped sum.
- Different areas need different questions: add an `Area` column to `Questions5S` and filter on it in the start formula.

## Common mistakes

- Letting the question list change while audits are running. Copy the text into the line, as shown.
- Averaging ratings that were skipped. The -1 marker and the answered filter prevent that, and the save button stays disabled until everything is rated.
- Comparing areas with different numbers of questions by raw points. Compare percentages.
- Turning the score into a league table between teams without discussion. Scores drive behaviour; agree what the audit is for first.

## Delegation notes

- `colLines` is a local collection, so Filter, Sum, CountIf and ForAll on it are evaluated in the app and have no delegation limit. The source `Questions5S` should stay below the data row limit (500 by default); a question list is far smaller.
- The ForAll page says records can be processed in any order and, when possible, in parallel, so do not rely on the order of the created `AuditLines` rows; every row carries its own question text and pillar for that reason. 20 to 60 questions are fine; for hundreds of rows look at the batch Patch pattern (the Patch page describes a multi-record form with a table of base records and a table of change records).
- `Errors()` is documented as returning errors of previous operations on a data source; the next data function on the same source clears them, and its page has no `ForAll` example. That is why the save formula collects failures itself. Test it with a forced failure.

## Privacy and safety

- The auditor email is personal data; audit results are about areas, not people. Do not add the name of the area owner to the lines.
- Photos of workplaces can show people, drawings or customer parts. Agree on rules for photos before you add them, and in aerospace areas check whether cameras are allowed at all.

title: Gemba walk capture app in Power Apps: observations, waste tags, photos and open actions
summary: Capture Gemba walk observations on a phone with SQDC and waste tags, photos through SharePoint attachments and mandatory owner and date for actions. Includes counts by waste type and a personal action list.
body:
A Gemba walk produces observations: a stack of notes on a clipboard, photos on a phone, and a list of promises that nobody can find a week later. This canvas app captures each observation as a record while you stand at the process, tags it with a waste type or an SQDC category, optionally attaches a photo, and turns "action needed" observations into a list with an owner and a date. At the end of the walk it shows a small count by waste type so the walk ends with a picture, not just a feeling.

## Prerequisites and version

- Power Apps canvas app on a phone or tablet, SharePoint connector (standard connector; check your license and tenant policy).
- Two SharePoint lists, see below. Photos use the Attachments feature of the SharePoint list through an edit form, which is the most robust way for SharePoint. For Dataverse you would use an Image column instead; check your table design.
- The eight wastes used here are the common lean list: Defects, Overproduction, Waiting, Non-utilised talent, Transportation, Inventory, Motion, Extra processing.

## Data model

List `GembaWalks`: `Title` (area and date, for example "Machining hall, 2026-11-20", this example date is invented), `WalkedBy` (text, email), `WalkDate` (date), `Purpose` (single line of text, for example "Follow up on setup times").

List `GembaObservations`:

| Column | Type | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Title | Single line of text | One short sentence, about the process, not about a person |
| WalkId | Number | ID of the GembaWalks row |
| Category | Choice | Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, People (SQDC) |
| Waste | Choice | The eight wastes plus "None, good practice" |
| Detail | Multiple lines of text | What you saw, how often, for how long |
| ActionRequired | Yes/No | |
| ActionOwner | Single line of text | Email of the person who agreed to the action |
| DueDate | Date | |
| Status | Choice | Open, Done, Dropped |
| WalkedBy | Single line of text | Copy of User().Email |

Turn on Attachments for `GembaObservations`. Add a column for good practice on purpose: a walk that only lists problems teaches people to hide the floor from you.

## Screens

`scrStart` (choose or create the walk), `scrCapture` (edit form plus counter), `scrSummary` (counts by waste and the action list).

## Formulas

Start a walk (`btnStartWalk.OnSelect`):

```powerfx
Set(
    varWalk,
    Patch(
        GembaWalks,
        Defaults(GembaWalks),
        {
            Title: txtArea.Text & ", " & Text(Today(), "yyyy-mm-dd"),
            WalkedBy: User().Email,
            WalkDate: Today(),
            Purpose: txtPurpose.Text
        }
    )
);
If(
    IsError(varWalk),
    Notify("The walk could not be created.", NotificationType.Error),
    ClearCollect(colWalkObs, Filter(GembaObservations, WalkId = varWalk.ID));
    Navigate(scrCapture, ScreenTransition.None)
)
```

Edit form for a new observation (`frmObs`): Mode `FormMode.New`, DataSource `GembaObservations`, cards for Title, Category, Waste, Detail, ActionRequired, ActionOwner, DueDate and Attachments. Set the hidden defaults in the card `Default` properties: the WalkId card `Default` to `varWalk.ID`, the WalkedBy card to `User().Email`, and for the Status Choice card set `DefaultSelectedItems` to `[{ Value: "Open" }]` (Choice cards use `DefaultSelectedItems`; the Learn form page does not cover data card properties, so check the card in the formula bar and test one submit).

Save button (`btnSaveObs.OnSelect`):

```powerfx
SubmitForm(frmObs)
```

Form behaviour properties:

```powerfx
// frmObs.OnSuccess
Collect(colWalkObs, frmObs.LastSubmit); // check: if the schema differs, reload with ClearCollect instead
NewForm(frmObs);
Notify("Observation saved", NotificationType.Success)

// frmObs.OnFailure
Notify("Not saved: " & frmObs.Error, NotificationType.Error)
```

Learn describes `LastSubmit` as the last successfully submitted record including server-generated fields such as the ID, available in `OnSuccess`. Whether its Choice columns have exactly the shape of the records already in `colWalkObs` depends on your list. The safe alternative is to reload after each successful submit: `ClearCollect(colWalkObs, Filter(GembaObservations, WalkId = varWalk.ID))`.

A rule that the owner and the date are mandatory when an action is requested (`DisplayMode` of the save button):

```powerfx
If(
    frmObs.Valid &&
    (!tglAction.Value || (!IsBlank(txtOwner.Text) && !IsBlank(dpDue.SelectedDate))),
    DisplayMode.Edit,
    DisplayMode.Disabled
)
```

Counter on the capture screen (`lblCount.Text`):

```powerfx
CountRows(colWalkObs) & " observations, " &
CountRows(Filter(colWalkObs, ActionRequired = true)) & " with action"
```

Summary by waste type (`galWaste.Items`), with the `As` operator to avoid mixing the choice value with the collection record:

```powerfx
SortByColumns(
    ForAll(
        Choices(GembaObservations.Waste) As c,
        {
            Waste: c.Value,
            N: CountRows(Filter(colWalkObs, Waste.Value = c.Value))
        }
    ),
    "N", SortOrder.Descending
)
```

My open actions across all walks (`galActions.Items`). Both conditions compare columns with constants, which SharePoint can evaluate on the server:

```powerfx
SortByColumns(
    Filter(
        GembaObservations,
        ActionRequired = true,
        Status.Value = "Open",
        ActionOwner = User().Email
    ),
    "DueDate", SortOrder.Ascending
)
```

## Worked example (invented data)

A 40 minute walk in a machining hall produces 12 observations: 10 with a waste type and 2 good practice entries that carry "None, good practice". Of the 10: Waiting 4 (three about missing material at the setup station, one about a crane), Motion 3 (tool search), Defects 2 (burrs found at the next station), Inventory 1. That is 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10, so the counts refer to the eight wastes only. Four observations are marked "action needed", each with an owner and a date within two weeks. The summary shows Waiting at 4 of 10, which is 40 percent of the problem observations, and supports the question "why does material arrive after the setup starts?" for the next A3. Twelve observations in 40 minutes is a sample of one walk, not a statistic about the hall. (The by-waste gallery also lists the row "None, good practice" with 2, because it loops over all choices.)

## How to adapt

- Voice notes: the form is typing-heavy on a phone. Add the Microphone control only after you have checked where audio is stored and who can listen to it.
- Follow-up: let a Power Automate flow create a Planner task from every new row with ActionRequired set, see the flow entries in the library.
- Different walk types (safety, quality, 5S): add a `WalkType` choice on `GembaWalks` and filter dropdowns by it.
- Shared walks: because `colWalkObs` is loaded once, call `Refresh(GembaObservations)` and reload it if two people walk together.

## Common mistakes

- Writing the name of an operator into the observation. A Gemba walk looks at the process; names turn it into an inspection and people start to hide problems.
- Choosing a waste for everything. Let "None, good practice" and "Other" exist, otherwise the counts are noise.
- Actions without an owner or date. The save-button rule above prevents that.
- Forgetting that attachments are stored in the list: set a storage and retention rule for the site.

## Delegation notes

- The Filter in `galActions` uses equality on a Yes/No column, equality on the Choice subfield and equality on a text column. SharePoint can delegate these; sorting by `DueDate` (a date column) is also delegable.
- `ForAll` over `Choices()` and `CountRows` over a collection run locally; the collection holds only one walk, so the size is no issue.
- Keep `GembaObservations` below the data row limit for unfiltered galleries, or always filter by WalkId or status.

## Privacy and safety

- Photos can show faces, name badges, screens and customer parts. Set a rule: no faces, no screens, no part numbers of customer-owned or export-controlled items unless your security policy allows it. In aerospace and defence areas check whether personal phones or tablets are allowed on the floor at all.
- Do not use the app to rate individuals. If the walk results flow into performance conversations, involve the works council before you start.
- Observation text is stored in SharePoint with the site's permissions. Restrict the site to the leadership and lean team.

title: Tool crib check-out and return app in Power Apps with barcode scan and calibration warning
summary: Scan a tool barcode, see status and calibration due date, and log issue and return with a who-has-what list. Uses the barcode reader control, Patch with IfError and a typed fallback; warns only, never releases a tool.
body:
In a tool crib the questions are always the same: who has the torque wrench, is its calibration still valid, and why is the crib counter full of people writing on a clipboard. This canvas app lets a mechanic scan the tool's barcode, checks status and calibration due date, and records the issue or the return with a time stamp and an optional work order reference. It gives you a live "who has what" list and an overdue-calibration list.

It is a convenience and a log. In regulated environments such as aviation maintenance the system of record for calibration and tool control is defined in your procedures (for a Part-145 organisation, the MOE). Check what your procedure requires before you let an app decide anything; this design only warns, it never releases a tool.

## Prerequisites and version

- Power Apps canvas app, SharePoint connector (standard connector; check your license). Choice values are written as `{ Value: "Out" }`, the shape commonly used for SharePoint Choice columns; the Learn Patch page documents only Dataverse enums, so test one Patch on your list.
- A phone or tablet. The current Barcode reader control is documented as supported on Android, iOS and Windows; the page says "Select to scan" is not supported in a web browser and does not state web support for the other modes, so test in the browser you use or plan a typed-input fallback. The older Barcode scanner control is marked as retired and does not scan in a browser.
- Barcode labels on the tools that carry the tool ID. Code 128 and Code 39 are supported on all three platforms according to the documentation.

## Data model

List `Tools`: `Title` (tool ID exactly as printed in the barcode, unique), `Description` (text), `Location` (text, home position), `Status` (Choice: Available, Out, Quarantine), `CalibrationDue` (date, blank if the tool needs no calibration), `HolderEmail` (text, blank when available).

List `ToolLog` (append only): `Title` (tool ID), `Action` (Choice: Issue, Return), `PersonEmail` (text), `WorkOrder` (text, optional), `Timestamp` (date and time), `Note` (text).

## Screens

`scrScan` with the barcode reader, a manual-entry textbox and a status panel; `scrOverview` with two galleries (tools out, calibration overdue).

## Formulas

Barcode reader `OnScan`. The control returns a table of barcodes; the documented formula for the text is `First(BarcodeReader.Barcodes).Value`:

```powerfx
Set(varToolId, Upper(Trim(First(BarcodeReader1.Barcodes).Value)));
Refresh(Tools);
Set(varTool, LookUp(Tools, Title = varToolId))
```

Manual fallback (`btnLookup.OnSelect`), same result for typed IDs:

```powerfx
Set(varToolId, Upper(Trim(txtToolId.Text)));
Refresh(Tools);
Set(varTool, LookUp(Tools, Title = varToolId))
```

`Upper` here only normalises the typed text; if your labels contain lower-case letters, drop it. `Refresh` pulls the current status so two people who scan the same tool within seconds do not both see "Available".

Warning text for the status panel (`lblState.Text`):

```powerfx
If(
    IsBlank(varToolId), "Scan a tool",
    IsBlank(varTool), "Unknown tool ID " & varToolId,
    varTool.Status.Value = "Quarantine", "Quarantined, do not issue",
    !IsBlank(varTool.CalibrationDue) && varTool.CalibrationDue < Today(),
        "Calibration overdue since " & Text(varTool.CalibrationDue, "yyyy-mm-dd"),
    varTool.Status.Value = "Out", "Out with " & varTool.HolderEmail,
    "Available"
)
```

Issue button, visible only when the tool is known, available and not overdue (`btnIssue.Visible`):

```powerfx
!IsBlank(varTool) &&
varTool.Status.Value = "Available" &&
(IsBlank(varTool.CalibrationDue) || varTool.CalibrationDue >= Today())
```

Issue action (`btnIssue.OnSelect`). The IfError chain stops at the first failure, as documented for chained actions:

```powerfx
IfError(
    Patch(
        ToolLog,
        Defaults(ToolLog),
        {
            Title: varTool.Title,
            Action: { Value: "Issue" },
            PersonEmail: User().Email,
            WorkOrder: txtWorkOrder.Text,
            Timestamp: Now()
        }
    ),
    Notify("Log entry failed: " & FirstError.Message, NotificationType.Error),
    Patch(
        Tools,
        varTool,
        { Status: { Value: "Out" }, HolderEmail: User().Email }
    ),
    Notify("Tool status failed: " & FirstError.Message & " Check the log entry.", NotificationType.Error),
    Notify("Issued " & varTool.Title, NotificationType.Success)
);
Set(varTool, Blank())
```

Return action follows the same pattern with `Action: { Value: "Return" }` and `Status: { Value: "Available" }, HolderEmail: ""`. Add a damage question before the return, and let the answer set `Status` to `Quarantine` instead of Available when the user reports damage.

Galleries on `scrOverview`:

```powerfx
// galOut.Items
SortByColumns(Filter(Tools, Status.Value = "Out"), "Title", SortOrder.Ascending)

// galOverdue.Items
SortByColumns(
    Filter(Tools, CalibrationDue < Today(), Status.Value <> "Quarantine"),
    "CalibrationDue", SortOrder.Ascending
)
```

## Worked example (invented data)

Tool T-1043 (torque wrench) has CalibrationDue 2026-12-01. On 2026-11-20 a mechanic scans it: the status is Available and the due date lies in the future, so the Issue button shows. After the Issue Patch, `Tools.Status` is Out and `HolderEmail` holds the mechanic. T-0877 (a micrometer) has CalibrationDue 2026-11-01. Scanning it on 2026-11-20 shows "Calibration overdue since 2026-11-01" and no Issue button. The overdue gallery lists it, and the metrology owner can see that it is 19 days past due (DateDiff of the due date and today in days). All identifiers and dates here are invented.

## How to adapt

- Tool kits with a set of items: add a `KitId` column and show missing items on return.
- Reminders: let a flow send the holder a message when a tool is out longer than your limit, instead of putting a timer into the app.
- Calibration data from your calibration system: import the due dates into `Tools` on a schedule; do not let people type them.
- No camera or no scanner: the typed fallback keeps the process usable; add a Power Apps component for repeated use.

## Common mistakes

- Treating the app as the calibration control. It displays a date someone entered. The record that matters is in the system your quality department designated.
- Skipping `Refresh` before the Patch. A stale status lets two people issue the same tool.
- Barcodes with trailing spaces or a different case than the `Title`. Trim on both sides when the data is imported.
- Patching `Tools` before the log entry. Write the log first so a failure still leaves a trace, as in the chain above.
- Using a lookup column for the tool in `ToolLog`. A text copy keeps old log entries readable when a tool is retired.

## Delegation notes

- `Title = varToolId` (equality on a text column) and `Status.Value = "Out"` are delegable to SharePoint according to the SharePoint delegation table on Learn. A comparison of a Date column with `Today()` is delegable too. The table also lists `<>` for complex (Choice) columns, but check for a delegation warning in the formula bar anyway; if one appears, replace it with an Or of the allowed values (`Not` does not delegate on SharePoint).
- `IsBlank` inside Filter is not delegable on SharePoint (the same table says so), which is why the formulas test blank values on the single record `varTool`, not inside a Filter. Note the blank `CalibrationDue` of tools without calibration: do not expect them in `galOverdue`, check that on your data.
- For a crib with several thousand tools keep the lists indexed on `Title` and `Status`; indexing is a SharePoint list setting, check it for your list.

## Privacy and safety

- The log records who borrowed what and when. That is employee data in many countries; involve the works council or data protection officer, define who may see the log, and set a retention period.
- A damaged or doubtful tool must be taken out of service by the person responsible under your procedure; the Quarantine status is only a flag.
- Keep tool IDs free of customer or aircraft information.

title: First article inspection checklist in Power Apps with tolerance pass/fail calculation
summary: A shopfloor checklist that loads characteristics per part and revision, compares measured values with nominal and tolerance using rounded deviations, and stores results. Not a replacement for formal first article reports.
body:
The first part of a new batch, a new revision or a new setup is where mistakes are cheapest to catch and most expensive to miss. Many shops still do the first-article check on a printed sheet, then re-type it. This canvas app guides the inspector through the characteristics for a part number, compares each measured value with nominal and tolerance, shows pass or fail immediately, and stores the result as a record linked to part, revision and work order.

Be clear about what it is: a shopfloor checklist and calculator. If your customer or your quality system requires a formal first article inspection report (in aerospace usually the AS9102 forms or a customer-specific equivalent), this app does not replace them and does not approve anything. It can feed the data into your formal process; check the exact requirements with your quality department.

## Prerequisites and version

- Power Apps canvas app, SharePoint connector (standard connector; check your license).
- A characteristics template per part number and revision, owned by quality or engineering, not by the shopfloor.
- Calibrated gauges and a defined procedure. The app compares numbers; it does not know whether the gauge was suitable.
- Choice values are written as `{ Value: "Submitted" }`, the shape commonly used for SharePoint Choice columns; the Learn Patch page documents only Dataverse enums, so test one Patch on your list.

## Data model

List `FAITemplates` (maintained by engineering): `Title` (part number), `Revision` (text), `CharNo` (number, the balloon number on the drawing), `Description` (text), `Nominal` (number), `TolMinus` (number, positive, allowed deviation below nominal), `TolPlus` (number, positive), `Unit` (text), `Gauge` (text, the gauge type required).

List `FAIRecords` (one row per inspection): `Title` (part number), `Revision`, `WorkOrder` (text), `Inspector` (text, email), `InspectionDate` (date and time), `Status` (Choice: Draft, Submitted, Accepted, Rejected), `HasFail` (Yes/No), `Decision` (multiple lines of text), `DecidedBy` (text, email).

List `FAIResults` (one row per characteristic): `Title` (part number), `RecordId` (number), `CharNo` (number), `Measured` (number), `Result` (text: Pass, Fail), `GaugeId` (text), `Comment` (text).

List `FAIApprovers`: `Title` (email of a person authorised to accept or reject first articles). Authorisation itself is decided in your quality system; this list only mirrors it.

## Formulas

Load the template (`btnLoad.OnSelect`). `If(false, 0)` creates a number column that starts blank; check in your app that the column is typed as a number and not as an untyped blank:

```powerfx
ClearCollect(
    colChars,
    AddColumns(
        Filter(FAITemplates, Title = txtPart.Text, Revision = txtRev.Text),
        "Measured", If(false, 0),
        "GaugeId", "",
        "Comment", ""
    )
);
If(
    IsEmpty(colChars),
    Notify("No template for this part and revision. Do not inspect without one.", NotificationType.Error),
    Navigate(scrMeasure, ScreenTransition.None)
)
```

A text input per row (`txtMeasured` inside the gallery over `colChars`), with `OnChange`:

```powerfx
UpdateIf(
    colChars,
    ID = ThisItem.ID,
    { Measured: If(IsBlank(txtMeasured.Text), Blank(), IfError(Value(txtMeasured.Text), Blank())) }
)
```

Set the text input `Format` to `TextFormat.Number`. Decimal separators follow the device language setting, so test on the real tablet. The `IfError` turns text that is not a number into a blank value, so the row stays unmeasured instead of raising an error.

Result label per row (`lblResult.Text`). The deviation is rounded before comparison because Power Apps numbers are floating point and a value exactly on the limit can otherwise land on the wrong side:

```powerfx
If(
    IsBlank(ThisItem.Measured),
    "",
    With(
        { dev: Round(ThisItem.Measured - ThisItem.Nominal, 4) },
        If(dev >= -ThisItem.TolMinus && dev <= ThisItem.TolPlus, "Pass", "Fail")
    )
)
```

Why the rounding matters, with a number checked in double-precision arithmetic (Python): 0.26 - 0.25 is 0.010000000000000009, which is greater than 0.01, so a raw comparison fails a measurement that sits exactly on the limit. Power Apps Number columns are described as floating point; test the same boundary in your app, and check the column type if you use a Decimal type. Test the rounding for your own resolution: if you measure to 0.001 and tolerances have three decimals, rounding to 4 decimals is safe; if you work in micrometres, choose a different `Round` depth. Colour the label with `If(Self.Text = "Fail", Color.Red, Color.Green)` and also show the word, so colour-blind users are covered.

Counters (`lblSummary.Text`), where results are recomputed locally with the same rule:

```powerfx
With(
    {
        done: CountRows(Filter(colChars, !IsBlank(Measured))),
        total: CountRows(colChars)
    },
    done & " of " & total & " measured"
)
```

Submit button, disabled until every characteristic has a value (`DisplayMode`):

```powerfx
If(CountIf(colChars, IsBlank(Measured)) = 0, DisplayMode.Edit, DisplayMode.Disabled)
```

Submit action (`btnSubmit.OnSelect`). `varHasFail` is set first from the local collection:

```powerfx
Set(
    varHasFail,
    CountRows(
        Filter(
            colChars,
            Round(Measured - Nominal, 4) < -TolMinus || Round(Measured - Nominal, 4) > TolPlus
        )
    ) > 0
);
Set(
    varFai,
    Patch(
        FAIRecords,
        Defaults(FAIRecords),
        {
            Title: txtPart.Text,
            Revision: txtRev.Text,
            WorkOrder: txtWO.Text,
            Inspector: User().Email,
            InspectionDate: Now(),
            Status: { Value: "Submitted" },
            HasFail: varHasFail
        }
    )
);
If(
    IsError(varFai),
    Notify("The inspection record was not saved.", NotificationType.Error),
    Clear(colFailed);
    ForAll(
        colChars,
        IfError(
            Patch(
                FAIResults,
                Defaults(FAIResults),
                {
                    Title: txtPart.Text,
                    RecordId: varFai.ID,
                    CharNo: ThisRecord.CharNo,
                    Measured: ThisRecord.Measured,
                    Result: If(
                        Round(ThisRecord.Measured - ThisRecord.Nominal, 4) >= -ThisRecord.TolMinus &&
                        Round(ThisRecord.Measured - ThisRecord.Nominal, 4) <= ThisRecord.TolPlus,
                        "Pass", "Fail"
                    ),
                    GaugeId: ThisRecord.GaugeId,
                    Comment: ThisRecord.Comment
                }
            ),
            Collect(colFailed, { CharNo: ThisRecord.CharNo, Msg: FirstError.Message })
        )
    );
    If(
        IsEmpty(colFailed),
        Notify(If(varHasFail, "Submitted with failures. Contact quality now.", "Submitted"), NotificationType.Information),
        Notify("Some results were not saved. The inspection is incomplete: tell quality, do not rely on it.", NotificationType.Error)
    )
)
```

`colFailed` is a helper collection created by the first `Collect`. A record whose result rows are missing must never be read as a complete inspection: compare the number of `FAIResults` rows with the number of template rows before anyone decides on it. The Learn pages do not describe `IfError`, `Collect` and `ForAll` together end to end, so force a failure on a test list and check that `colFailed` fills.

Decision screen, available only to approvers (`btnDecide.Visible`):

```powerfx
!IsBlank(LookUp(FAIApprovers, Title = User().Email))
```

## Worked example (invented data)

Part "PN-4711" revision B, six characteristics. Characteristic 3 is a bore: nominal 25.000, TolMinus 0.020, TolPlus 0.020. The inspector measures 25.014: deviation 0.014, within plus 0.020, so Pass. Characteristic 5 is a length: nominal 120.50, TolMinus 0.10, TolPlus 0.10, measured 120.63: deviation 0.13 is above 0.10, so Fail. The other four pass. The submit formula sets `HasFail` to true, the record gets Status Submitted, and the message tells the inspector to contact quality. A person on `FAIApprovers` then sets Rejected or Accepted with a written decision. The app never makes that decision itself.

## How to adapt

- Attribute checks (visual, label present, certificate attached): add a column `CheckType` (Variable or Attribute) to the template and switch the input control between number box and Pass/Fail toggle.
- One-sided tolerances: store upper and lower limits instead of nominal and plus/minus, and compare directly.
- Link to the NCR process: when `HasFail` is true, start the nonconformance flow with part, revision and work order prefilled.
- Gauge control: fill `GaugeId` by scanning, and warn when a gauge is overdue, see the tool crib entry.

## Common mistakes

- Letting the shopfloor edit the templates. A changed tolerance in the template silently changes what "Pass" means.
- Mixing units. Store the unit with the characteristic and show it on every row.
- Comparing without rounding. In double-precision arithmetic 0.26 - 0.25 is 0.010000000000000009, so a measured 0.260 against nominal 0.250 plus 0.010 fails the raw comparison although it sits exactly on the limit. The `Round` guard handles it, but still test the boundary cases with your own values and your column types.
- Treating a pass in the app as released. Release and acceptance stay with the authorised person under your procedure.
- Not versioning the template. Use part number plus revision as the key, as above.

## Delegation notes

- The Filter on the template uses equality on two text columns, which SharePoint can delegate. Keep template rows per part small; the load formula pulls them into a collection.
- All pass or fail arithmetic runs on the collection in the app, so there is no delegation limit, but one inspection with several hundred characteristics will feel slow on a tablet; split it by drawing sheet.
- `CountIf` and `Filter` on a collection are evaluated locally. `LookUp(FAIApprovers, ...)` is a small list lookup.

## Privacy and safety

- Inspector email and time stamp are personal data; limit who can read `FAIRecords`.
- Measurement data can be export-controlled or customer proprietary. Put the lists on a site with restricted access, and check data location rules in your contracts.
- Keep the formal inspection records in the system your quality department designated; treat this app's lists as working data unless quality says otherwise.

title: MRO shift handover app in Power Apps: six categories, nothing-to-report rule and acknowledgement
summary: A structured handover per aircraft or work order with six categories, an explicit nothing-to-report line, urgent flags and acknowledgement by the incoming shift. A communication record, not a maintenance record or release.
body:
Shift handover in a hangar or a production hall fails in a predictable way: the information exists, but it sits in somebody's head, in a notebook, or in a verbal chat at the gate. This canvas app structures the handover per aircraft or per work order: what was completed, what is still open, new defects, closed defects, parts and material, and general issues. Each category must either contain at least one line or carry an explicit "nothing to report", because silence is ambiguous. The incoming shift acknowledges the handover in the app, so you can see who knew what and when.

It is a communication record. It is not a maintenance record, not a certificate of release and not a substitute for work cards, task sign-offs or defect entries in your maintenance information system. Those stay in their own systems, and certifying staff stay responsible for what they certify. The app can reference card numbers; it must not replace them.

## Regulatory background (check before you rely on it)

A manufacturer's trade article (not an official source) states that for Part-145 organisations the rule 145.A.47(c) requires relevant information to be handed over at shift and task changes, that the procedure belongs in the Maintenance Organisation Exposition (MOE), and that the handover is made per aircraft registration and work order. It also names typical contents: completed planned work, open work, new and closed defect cards, open parts and material, general issues, and it treats "nothing to report" as information. Check the paragraph, wording and retention periods against the current regulation and your own MOE; do not take the numbers from this entry. Outside aviation the same structure still works for any multi-shift line.

## Prerequisites and version

- Power Apps canvas app, SharePoint connector (standard connector; check your license). Tablet layout works best. Choice values are written as `{ Value: "Draft" }`, the shape commonly used for SharePoint Choice columns; the Learn Patch page documents only Dataverse enums, so test one Patch on your list.
- Two SharePoint lists and an agreed handover procedure that quality has approved.
- Wi-Fi coverage where the handover happens. Power Apps can store data locally with `SaveData` and `LoadData` on mobile devices; offline use and the security of locally stored data depend on your environment and device management, so check the current documentation and your IT policy before you use it for anything beyond a draft.

## Data model

List `Handovers`: `Title` (registration or work order reference, text; use your own convention), `WorkOrder` (text), `FromShift` (Choice: Early, Late, Night, your own list), `ToShift` (Choice), `HandoverDate` (date), `Author` (text, email), `Status` (Choice: Draft, Handed over, Acknowledged), `AcknowledgedBy` (text, email), `AcknowledgedOn` (date and time).

List `HandoverLines`: `Title` (short text of the item), `HandoverId` (number, ID of the Handovers row), `Category` (text: one of the six names below), `Reference` (text, for example work card or defect number), `Priority` (Choice: Normal, Urgent), `Detail` (multiple lines of text), `NothingToReport` (Yes/No; when true the line carries no detail).

The six categories used here: Completed work, Open work, New defects, Closed defects, Parts and material, General issues.

## Formulas

Initialise a new handover (`scrEdit.OnVisible`):

```powerfx
ClearCollect(colLines, Filter(HandoverLines, HandoverId = varHandover.ID));
ClearCollect(
    colCats,
    Table(
        { Cat: "Completed work" },
        { Cat: "Open work" },
        { Cat: "New defects" },
        { Cat: "Closed defects" },
        { Cat: "Parts and material" },
        { Cat: "General issues" }
    )
)
```

If you create a brand new handover, set `varHandover` first with a Patch on `Handovers` using `Defaults(Handovers)` and `Status: { Value: "Draft" }`, as in the downtime entry.

Add a line (`btnAddLine.OnSelect`):

```powerfx
Collect(
    colLines,
    {
        Title: txtTitle.Text,
        Category: ddCat.Selected.Cat,
        Reference: txtRef.Text,
        Priority: { Value: If(tglUrgent.Value, "Urgent", "Normal") },
        Detail: txtDetail.Text,
        NothingToReport: false
    }
);
Reset(txtTitle); Reset(txtRef); Reset(txtDetail)
```

"Nothing to report" button for the category selected in the list (`btnNothing.OnSelect`):

```powerfx
Collect(
    colLines,
    {
        Title: "Nothing to report",
        Category: ddCat.Selected.Cat,
        Reference: "",
        Priority: { Value: "Normal" },
        Detail: "",
        NothingToReport: true
    }
)
```

Categories that still have no line (`galMissing.Items`; use the same formula inside the hand-over button):

```powerfx
Filter(
    colCats As c,
    CountRows(Filter(colLines, Category = c.Cat)) = 0
)
```

Hand-over button (`btnHandover.OnSelect`), disabled while `CountRows(galMissing.Items) > 0`. Only lines without an ID are written, so lines that were loaded from a saved draft are not duplicated. Failures are collected per line with `IfError` into the helper collection `colFailed` (created by the first `Collect`):

```powerfx
If(
    CountRows(Filter(colCats As c, CountRows(Filter(colLines, Category = c.Cat)) = 0)) > 0,
    Notify("Every category needs a line or 'Nothing to report'.", NotificationType.Warning),
    Clear(colFailed);
    ForAll(
        Filter(colLines, IsBlank(ID)),
        IfError(
            Patch(
                HandoverLines,
                Defaults(HandoverLines),
                {
                    Title: ThisRecord.Title,
                    HandoverId: varHandover.ID,
                    Category: ThisRecord.Category,
                    Reference: ThisRecord.Reference,
                    Priority: ThisRecord.Priority,
                    Detail: ThisRecord.Detail,
                    NothingToReport: ThisRecord.NothingToReport
                }
            ),
            Collect(colFailed, { Line: ThisRecord.Title, Msg: FirstError.Message })
        )
    );
    If(
        IsEmpty(colFailed),
        Patch(Handovers, varHandover, { Status: { Value: "Handed over" } });
        Notify("Handed over", NotificationType.Success);
        Navigate(scrHome),
        Notify(CountRows(colFailed) & " lines were not saved. Do not tap again, call your supervisor.", NotificationType.Error)
    )
)
```

Check that this runs once per handover; if the user taps again after a partial failure, the lines that did save would be written a second time, because the local collection rows still have no ID. The Learn pages do not describe `IfError`, `Collect` and `ForAll` together end to end, so force a failure on a test list first. In production, write the lines one by one when they are added and use the button only to change the status.

Acknowledgement by the incoming shift (`btnAck.OnSelect`). The author cannot acknowledge their own handover:

```powerfx
If(
    User().Email = ThisItem.Author,
    Notify("The incoming shift must acknowledge.", NotificationType.Warning),
    IfError(
        Patch(
            Handovers,
            ThisItem,
            {
                Status: { Value: "Acknowledged" },
                AcknowledgedBy: User().Email,
                AcknowledgedOn: Now()
            }
        ),
        Notify("Not saved: " & FirstError.Message, NotificationType.Error),
        Notify("Acknowledged", NotificationType.Success)
    )
)
```

Gallery of handovers waiting for the incoming shift (`galIncoming.Items`):

```powerfx
SortByColumns(
    Filter(Handovers, Status.Value = "Handed over", HandoverDate >= DateAdd(Today(), -1, TimeUnit.Days)),
    "HandoverDate", SortOrder.Descending
)
```

## Worked example (invented data)

Late shift hands over a work package (invented reference "WP-0042"). Completed work: 2 lines. Open work: 3 lines, one with Reference "card 17" and priority Urgent because a part is due at 06:00. New defects: 1 line. Closed defects: "Nothing to report". Parts and material: 1 line (one fastener kit still missing). General issues: "Nothing to report". That is 2 + 3 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 9 lines, and the two "Nothing to report" lines are real entries, so the six-category check passes. The night shift opens the handover, sees the Urgent line first (if you sort the line gallery by priority; the sample formulas do not do that), acknowledges it at 22:05, and the Handovers row shows who acknowledged and when. The notice that the missing kit blocks card 17 is now in writing, not in a corridor conversation.

## How to adapt

- One handover per aircraft or per line: change the `Title` convention and the filter in `galIncoming`.
- Links to defect and card systems: store the reference as text; add a hyperlink only if your system has stable URLs.
- Notifications: let a flow tell the incoming shift lead when a handover is created, see the shift handover reminder entry in the library.
- Different categories for production: replace the six names with your own and keep the "nothing to report" rule.

## Common mistakes

- Treating the app as the record of work done. Task completion and release stay in the maintenance system.
- Allowing an empty handover. The six-category check exists for that reason.
- Free text without a reference. A line "part missing" with no card number cannot be acted on.
- Letting the author acknowledge. The rule above prevents it in the app only; anyone with edit rights on the list can still change the status in SharePoint, so back the rule with list permissions or a flow that checks it.
- Keeping the handover verbal "because it is faster". The app only helps if the verbal part comes second.

## Delegation notes

- The incoming-shift gallery filters on a Choice subfield (equality) and a Date column compared with a constant. The SharePoint delegation table on Learn lists both as delegable; `DateAdd(Today(), ...)` should count as a constant, but check the formula bar for a delegation warning. `colLines` and `colCats` are local collections, so Filter and CountRows on them have no delegation limit.
- `Errors()` is documented as returning errors of previous operations, cleared by the next data function on the same source, with no `ForAll` example. The formulas above therefore collect failures per line themselves; verify the behaviour with a forced failure.
- `ForAll` may process records in any order and in parallel (ForAll page), so line order in the list is not guaranteed; keep a sequence number column if the order matters. For long handovers consider writing lines when they are added.

## Privacy and safety

- Lines can contain names, registration numbers and customer information. Restrict the site, and set a retention rule in line with your MOE and your data protection officer.
- Do not write medical or personal remarks about colleagues into the general issues category. Fatigue and staffing concerns belong in the safety reporting system.
- If handovers are evaluated by person (who writes long or short notes), involve the works council first.
